ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $4.41 to the rider (RD-2, NS-7); record the F4 segment as an unexcused route deviation on the driver's file; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F7: base $3.90 + distance $31.84 for 22.58 km + time $8.91 + platform $1.47 = $46.12), so extra kilometres feed straight into the fare and relief is measured per RD-2, not by the fixed-quote branch [F7][RD-2]. The trace settles that two off-route segments exist (F3, F4) and that only one of them is excused, so the review is segment by segment [F3][F4][RD-1].

Segment F3 (21:42–21:49, 4.26 km driven vs 1.57 km optimal, +2.69 km, up to 1084 m off the optimal route) is exempt: an LTA accident was reported at 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway towards TPE after Sheares Avenue Exit, 0 m from the optimal route, i.e. on the very stretch replaced, reported before the segment's 21:42 start and still listed in the trip window [F12][RD-4]. The speed-band records (PIE band 5, KLE band 4, 21:26–22:17) are not band 1 or 2, so they corroborate congestion only and cannot exempt a segment on their own, but they do not disturb the F3 exemption [F10][F11][RD-4]. No refund is due on the 2.69 km in F3.

Segment F4 (22:02–22:09, 4.57 km driven vs 1.43 km optimal, +3.13 km, up to 997 m off the optimal route) has no qualifying incident: F12 ties the single 21:26 accident to the KLE stretch already covered by F3, and nothing in F10–F12 ties an incident or a band ≤ 2 to the optimal road this second deviation replaced [F4][F12][RD-4]. The rider's agreement to that reroute is absent: there are no in-app chat messages at all (F8), and the only account of the driver "going round" the incident comes from his own statement written after the trip (F9) — a driver's claim of agreement in his statement is not rider consent (G11), and no rider message sent before 22:02 exists at all, so the reading is "counts" rather than undetermined [F8][F9][RD-5]. No rider-requested stop exists in this segment for RD-3 to excuse [F4][F3][RD-3].

Amount: the trace fixes the per-km rate at the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km, $31.84 ÷ 22.58 km = $1.4101/km, and RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of non-exempt segments [F5][F7][RD-2]. 3.13 km × $1.4101/km = $4.4146, rounded to $4.41. The greater $9.45 / 6.70 km excess in F5 is not awarded because RD-2 does not refund the exempt segment's kilometres nor the unallocated mapping-noise remainder, and no waiting or cancellation item arises (waiting $0.00, no cancellation fee) [F5][F6][F7][RD-2].

No account action: RD-6 requires a route violation established here plus route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in the window (his single upheld dispute is not a route case), so the "repeated" predicate is absent [F15][RD-6]. The rider's own profile (2 disputes, 0 upheld) decides nothing either way [F14][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: LTA accident reported 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway (towards TPE) after Sheares Avenue Exit, 0 m from the optimal route, i.e. on the replaced stretch, before this segment's 21:42 start and inside the trip window — the reasonable-cause exception in RD-4(a) applies; the band-4 record is corroboration only under RD-4(b). [F3][F12][F11][RD-4]

No qualifying incident ties to the optimal road this segment replaced (the single 21:26 report was used for F3) and the bands are not ≤ 2, so RD-4(c) sends it to RD-2; no rider message before 22:02 exists (F8 is empty) and the driver's post-trip statement (F9) is not rider consent, so RD-5 does not exempt it. [F4][F8][F9][F12][RD-4][RD-5][RD-3]

rejected_claims.reason: Withdrawn by the rider in rebuttal; F12 places the reported accident on the very stretch segment F3 replaced, before the 21:42 start, so the segment is exempt under RD-4(a) and no refund is due on its 2.69 km. [F3][F12][RD-4]
Withdrawn in rebuttal; RD-2 refunds only non-exempt segments' extra_km, so the $8.21 sum (2.69 + 3.13 km) is unavailable — the 2.69 km in F3 is exempt. [F3][F4][F5][RD-2]

Withdrawn in rebuttal; F15 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (the single upheld dispute is not a route case), so RD-6's repeated-breach predicate is not made out and no account flag attaches. [F15][RD-6]
Not relied on by the driver in rebuttal; F14 (2 disputes, 0 upheld) is a profile fact that cannot decide the deviation either way. [F14][RD-6]

As originally pleaded it claimed segment F4's or both segments' exemption; RD-4(a) is a per-segment test and the F12 report is exhausted by F3, so it cannot exempt the 22:02–22:09 segment. [F3][F4][F12][RD-4]

Its assertion that no rider consent is needed because consent was never claimed does not exempt F4: with no RD-4 cause and no rider agreement before 22:02, the segment remains unexcused. [F4][F8][F9][RD-4][RD-5]

Its denial of flag_account is accepted, but not for the reason that no violation is established here — F4's deviation is established; the flag fails only because RD-6's prior-upheld-route-dispute element is absent. [F4][F15][RD-6]
